findings.title: A log read error is shown over whichever log is selected and never cleared
findings.claim: Read failures (and the oversize fallback) are pushed as { ok:false, error } with no logName; the page writes the message into the single logs pane regardless of the selected log, replacing its lines until that file next changes.

evidence.detail:
Make the ngrok log unreadable while scheduler is selected; the error event replaces the scheduler tail, and state.logTailsByLogName is not re-rendered.
Verifier: Merged blind and informed findings; confirmed by reading sendLogTail and startServerTab onError handler (showMessage with no log check). Checked by reading the code at d8a5dc5.

recommendation.reason: Cheap to fix by adding logName to the error event and ignoring it for unselected logs, and it makes the pane show wrong content.

findings.title: Documented order of the subscribe reply and first log pushes is the reverse of what the host does
findings.claim: docs/sifty-server-extension.md says the host replies isSubscribed then pushes tails, but subscribe() writes five logTail events synchronously before runNativeHostAsync writes the reply.

evidence.detail:
subscribe -> sendLogTail -> writeReplyAsync reaches output.write synchronously; the reply is written only after handleNativeHostMessageAsync returns.
Verifier: Current client ignores the reply so nothing breaks. Checked by reading the code at d8a5dc5.

recommendation.reason: Fixing the one doc sentence is trivial and the docs are currently wrong.

findings.title: Reversing physical lines turns multi-line entries such as stack traces upside down
findings.claim: showLog reverses lines, not entries, so continuation lines of a stack trace appear above its first line.

evidence.detail:
['Error: boom','  at a','  at b'] renders as '  at b\n  at a\nError: boom'.
Verifier: Newest-first is the stated intent of the branch; this is a trade-off of that choice, not a defect in it. Checked by reading the code at d8a5dc5.

resolution.note: Newest-first by line is the intended behaviour and entry grouping would need log format knowledge

recommendation.reason: Newest-first by line is the intended behaviour and entry grouping would need log format knowledge.
recommendation.reopenIf: Stack traces in the logs become common enough to be hard to read.

findings.title: Log stream opens at start-up even when the tab starts hidden
findings.claim: startServerTab calls openLogStream() unconditionally, so a tab loaded in the background holds a host process and five 250 ms pollers until first shown and hidden again, contrary to the docs.

evidence.detail:
Line 234 is a bare openLogStream() with no document.hidden check, unlike onPollTick.
Verifier: Merged the start-hidden halves of two findings. Checked by reading the code at d8a5dc5.

recommendation.reason: A one-line document.hidden guard removes wasted CPU and a stray host process.

findings.title: Chrome's disconnect reason is discarded
findings.claim: onDisconnect always reports 'Lost the connection to the native host' and never reads chrome.runtime.lastError, so host-not-found, forbidden and host-exited are indistinguishable and Chrome logs an unchecked-lastError warning.

evidence.detail:
The listener takes no arguments and builds a constant HostUnreachableError.
Verifier: Code confirmed; the lastError warning is plausible Chrome behaviour but not checked live. Checked by reading the code at d8a5dc5.

resolution.note: Real diagnostic loss but only affects error messages and is separable from this feature

recommendation.reason: Real diagnostic loss but only affects error messages and is separable from this feature.
recommendation.reopenIf: Users report confusing 'Live logs stopped' messages that hide the actual cause.

findings.title: Unknown stream events are dropped silently
findings.claim: handleLogStreamMessage returns without comment for any ok message whose event is not 'logTail', so a protocol change disappears with no signal.

evidence.detail:
The subscribeLogs acknowledgement { ok:true, isSubscribed:true } has no event field and arrives on the same port, so ignoring non-logTail messages is required.
Verifier: Raised as a no-silent-failures concern; the code path is deliberate. Checked by reading the code at d8a5dc5.

resolution.note: The subscribe acknowledgement legitimately has no event, so ignoring it is correct and the host and client ship together

recommendation.reason: The subscribe acknowledgement legitimately has no event, so ignoring it is correct and the host and client ship together.
recommendation.reopenIf: A new push event type is added to the host.

findings.title: A dropped stream leaves stale tails that render as live when another log is chosen
findings.claim: handleLogStreamClosed keeps logTailsByLogName, so after a drop choosing another log renders its old tail with no stopped notice until the 30 s reconnect.

evidence.detail:
showSelectedLog renders state.logTailsByLogName[selected] without checking state.logStream.
Verifier: Confirmed by reading showSelectedLog and handleLogStreamClosed; window is at most 30 s. Checked by reading the code at d8a5dc5.

resolution.note: Real but short-lived and the data is only seconds stale

recommendation.reason: Real but short-lived and the data is only seconds stale.
recommendation.reopenIf: Users act on stale log lines after a drop.
